action_items: Info for main agent: AV271676A7 IS currently premium per test_credentials.md and /api/payment/status → has_premium=true. The review_request stated 'NOT actually premium' which appears stale. Consequence: the user sees the unlocked Peer Comparison view WITHOUT ?demo=true. This is not a bug, but the unlocked state assertion for non-premium could not be tested with this user. To verify the premium-gated lock UI (upgrade-cta), use a fresh non-premium user or toggle has_premium=false in DB.

(Non-blocking) Console shows repeated 405 errors on Dashboard load — does not affect core flows but worth investigating in a future iteration. Look for any fetch/PATCH/PUT hitting an endpoint that only accepts GET.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/services/peer_comparison.py compare_with_peers (L63): uses questionnaire['city_tier'] directly but user.city from the users collection is separate. If users fill questionnaire without city_tier, defaults to tier_2 silently. Consider deriving city_tier from users.city when absent so the fallback is data-driven, not hard-coded.

/app/backend/server.py /reports/peer-comparison (L505-511): no caching — every request recomputes. For a benchmark-heavy report used by Dashboard CTA navigations, consider caching the result keyed by (user_id, questionnaire_updated_at) for 5-10 minutes to reduce MongoDB round-trips.

/app/frontend/src/components/OnboardingModal.js handleBulkScan (L54-69): timeout=300000 (5 min) — good, but no progress indicator beyond 'scanning'. If user closes tab mid-scan, localStorage.onboardingInProgress persists across sessions with no TTL. Consider adding a timestamp-based expiry.

/app/frontend/src/pages/PeerComparison.js: premium gate relies on a client-side check. Even if UI is locked, the GET /api/reports/peer-comparison endpoint itself does NOT enforce has_premium — any authenticated user with a questionnaire can call it directly. If peer-comparison is meant to be premium-only, add a server-side has_premium check in server.py:499 (like /api/reports/arthmitra pattern).

/app/backend/services/peer_comparison.py _age_bracket (L11-20): returns '25-29' for any age<30 including teenagers; returns '60+' as the top bracket but the benchmarks also have 60+ entries. For age<25 the synthetic data doesn't really apply — consider explicit handling (e.g., use 25-29 bracket but note 'limited data for <25').
